paragraphs: We are a local Bermuda company incorporated under the laws of Bermuda, incorporated on October 22, 1904, pursuant to The N.T. Butterfield & Son Bank Act, 1904 (the "Butterfield Act"). We are registered with the Registrar of Companies in Bermuda under registration number LC 2106. Our registered office and principal executive offices are located at 65 Front Street, Hamilton, HM 12, Bermuda. Our agent for service of process in the United States is C T Corporation System, 28 Liberty Street, New York, New York 10005. Our telephone number is (441) 295 1111. We maintain a website at www.butterfieldgroup.com. Neither this website nor the information on or accessible through this website is included or incorporated in, or is a part of, this report.
The SEC maintains an internet site at https://www.sec.gov that contains reports, information statements, and other information regarding issuers that file electronically with the SEC.

The origin of The Bank of N.T. Butterfield & Son Limited dates back to the founding of the trading firm of Nathaniel Butterfield circa 1784. In 1858, our company was established as a bank in Bermuda and has been instrumental to the functioning of the local economy ever since. The Bank was later incorporated under a special act of the local Parliament in 1904. In the 1960s, as international businesses began contributing substantially to Bermuda's economy, we developed services to work to meet their needs. In 1967, we opened offices in the Cayman Islands and by the 1980s had expanded our operations to include retail banking, investment management, and fund administration. In 1973, we opened our Guernsey office in order to provide customers with access to the Pound Sterling currency after Bermuda's departure from the British Sterling zone. In addition to being Bermuda's first bank, we opened the first ATMs in Bermuda in the 1980s and launched Bermuda's first internet banking service in 2001. In 1971, we listed our common shares on the BSX under the ticker symbol "NTB.BH". In 2016, we listed our common shares on the NYSE under the ticker symbol "NTB".

In 2008 and 2009, as a result of the global financial crisis, we realized losses attributable primarily to US non-agency mortgage backed securities in our investment portfolio, as well as write-downs on local market hospitality loans. To raise capital to offset these losses, the Bank executed a $200 million preference share offering in June 2009. In 2009 and 2010, we implemented a comprehensive restructuring plan for the Company: we hired a new management team, de-risked our balance sheet, and raised $550 million of common equity from a group of investors as well as existing shareholders.

Since our restructuring, we have pursued a strategy to focus on our core business in banking and wealth management. We have executed upon our strategy by streamlining the Company's operations through exiting non-core markets, repositioning our balance sheet, investing in efficiency initiatives, and continuing to invest in our core business lines to grow both organically and through acquisitions. By following this strategy, we have improved our financial results and have been able to initiate a progressive capital return policy for investors. The following are the most recent key steps in executing our strategy:

•In October 2017, we entered into an agreement to acquire Deutsche Bank AG's ("Deutsche Bank's") Global Trust Solutions ("GTS") business, excluding its US operations, for net cash payments of $24.7 million. Upon completion of the transaction, Butterfield took over the ongoing management and administration of the GTS portfolio, comprising approximately 1,000 trust structures for some 900 private clients in Guernsey, Switzerland, the Cayman Islands and Singapore. As part of the transaction, we also acquired a service company in Mauritius to provide operations and support services to our trust businesses. This transaction was completed in March 2018.

•In February 2018, we entered into an agreement to acquire Deutsche Bank's banking and custody business in the Cayman Islands and the Channel Islands, which provides services primarily to financial intermediaries and corporate clients. The Bank began to onboard certain customer deposits relating to the acquisition in 2018, and this onboarding activity was completed in the first half of 2019.
•In May 2018, we issued $75 million of 5.25% Fixed to Floating Rate Subordinated Notes due in 2028 to repay a portion of our outstanding indebtedness and for other general corporate purposes.

•In July 2019, we completed the £160.7 million ($201.1 million) acquisition of ABN AMRO (Channel Islands) Limited ("ABN AMRO (Channel Islands)"), which provides banking, investment management and custody products to three distinct client groups, including trusts, private clients, and funds.

•In June 2020, we issued $100 million of 5.25% Fixed to Floating Rate Subordinated Notes due in 2030 for general corporate purposes, including the repayment of a portion of our previously outstanding debt.

•In September 2022, we entered into an agreement to acquire assets from the Credit Suisse global trust businesses operating in Singapore, Guernsey and The Bahamas. The transaction was completed in December 2023.
•In June 2023, we executed the early redemption of the Bank's $75 million 5.25% Fixed to Floating Rate Subordinated Notes due June 1, 2028.

•In 2024, Butterfield's business in the Channel Islands was reorganized so that all business formerly carried on in or from within Jersey by Butterfield Bank (Jersey) Limited has been transferred to Butterfield Bank (Guernsey) Limited acting through its Jersey branch (Butterfield Bank (Guernsey) Limited, Jersey Branch). The scheme was sanctioned by the Royal Court of Jersey on May 14, 2024 and the transfer of the Business became effective on June 1, 2024.
•In June 2025, we executed the early redemption of the Bank's $100 million 5.25% Fixed to Floating Rate Subordinated Notes due June 15, 2030.

headings: Risks Relating to the Markets in Which We Operate
Macroeconomic factors, including regional conflicts, and other geopolitical events could disrupt our businesses and adversely affect our financial condition or results of operations.
A decline in tourism in Bermuda and the Cayman Islands could adversely affect our business, financial condition or results of operations.
Certain jurisdictions in which we operate, including Bermuda, Guernsey and Jersey, have a Deposit Insurance Scheme or Deposit Compensation Scheme and we incur ongoing costs as a result.
Severe weather, natural disasters and potential impacts of climate change could disrupt our businesses and adversely affect our financial condition or results of operations.
The majority of the markets in which we operate do not have systemic credit bureau reports.
Risks Relating to Our Strategy, Brand, Portfolio and Other Aspects of Our Business
We rely on our reputation and the appeal of our brand to our customers. Any damage to our reputation and appeal could harm us and our business prospects.
The effects of inflation, and volatility in interest rates have and may continue to negatively impact our net interest margin and our profitability.
Elevated levels of inflation could pose a risk to our financial performance.
Our loan and investment portfolios are subject to risk of prepayment, which could have a material adverse effect on us.
The value of the securities in our investment portfolio may decline in the future.
Volatility levels and fluctuations in foreign currency exchange rates may affect our business, financial position and results of operations.
If we are unable to effectively manage our liquidity we may need to seek additional financing and our business, financial condition or results of operations could be adversely affected.
We rely on third parties to provide services that are integral to our ordinary operations, and their failure to perform in a satisfactory manner could negatively affect us.
We face competition in all aspects of our business, and may not be able to attract and retain wealth management, trust and banking clients at current levels.
The addition of new products and services, or modified products or services may subject us to implementation risk and harm our reputation.
paragraphs: The material risks and uncertainties that management believes affect us are described below. Any of the following risks, as well as risks that we do not know of or currently deem immaterial, could have a material adverse effect on our business, financial condition or results of operations. Further, the risk factors below include cautionary statements identifying important factors that could cause actual results to differ materially from those expressed in any forward-looking statements made by us or on our behalf. See "Cautionary Note Regarding Forward-Looking Statements."

Adverse economic and market conditions in Bermuda, the Cayman Islands, the Channel Islands and the UK, and other markets in which we operate, have in the past resulted in and could in the future result in lower revenue, lower asset quality, increased provisions and lower earnings.

Our financial performance generally, and in particular the ability of our borrowers to pay interest and repay principal on outstanding loans and the value of the collateral securing those loans, as well as demand for loans and other products and services we offer and whose success we rely on to drive our future growth, are highly dependent upon the business environment in the markets in which we operate. A downturn in any of Bermuda, the Cayman Islands, or the Channel Islands and the UK can have a profound impact on our business performance. Some elements of the business environment that affect our financial performance include short-term and long-term interest rates, any downgrade in sovereign credit ratings to which our credit ratings are correlated, the prevailing yield curve, inflation and price levels, monetary and fiscal policy, regulatory or legal changes (including changes in tax, property and domiciliation laws and regulations) or changes in enforcement thereof, the imposition of tariffs or retaliatory tariffs, unemployment rates, investor or business confidence, natural or man-made disasters, the strength of the local economy in the markets in which we operate, or a combination of these or other factors. For example, the 2025 downgrade by Moody's and the 2023 downgrade by Fitch Rating Services of the US Long-Term Foreign-Currency Issuer Default Rating to 'Aa1' from "Aaa' and to 'AA+' from 'AAA', respectively, impacted the ratings on the Banks' holdings of US government treasuries and mortgage-backed securities issued by US governmental agencies. Any further downgrades could further affect the stability of securities issued or guaranteed by the federal government and the valuation or liquidity of our portfolio of such investment securities, and could result in our counterparties requiring additional collateral for our borrowings.

Unfavorable market conditions can result in a deterioration in the credit quality of our borrowers and the demand for our products and services, an increase in the number of loan delinquencies, defaults and charge-offs, additional provisions for loan losses, decreases in asset values, deterioration in investment performance and an overall material adverse effect on the quality of our loan portfolio.

Unlike banks that are more geographically diversified, our business is concentrated primarily in Bermuda, the Cayman Islands, and the Channel Islands and the UK, and we may be more affected by a downturn in these markets than more diversified competitors.

Our banking operations are concentrated in Bermuda, the Cayman Islands and the Channel Islands and the UK, and we serve customers in these markets. In the year ended December 31, 2025, 43%, 31% and 18%, of our total net revenue was derived from our Bermuda, Cayman, and Channel Islands and UK segments, respectively. In addition, in the year ended December 31, 2025, 33%, 23% and 44%, of our loans originated in Bermuda, Cayman, and Channel Islands and the UK, respectively. Accordingly, a downturn in these markets may have a profound effect on our banking business. In addition, we have sought to expand our core business lines, including through acquisitions. Any failure in our ability to expand our core business lines, successfully integrate acquisitions or any reduction in demand for our core services in our Bermuda, Cayman or Channel Islands and UK segments, including due to perceived reputational harm, increasing regulatory scrutiny over activities in these jurisdictions or otherwise, may adversely impact our business and results of operations, including the ongoing success of any of our acquired businesses.

paragraphs: This section presents management's perspective on our financial condition and results of operations. The following discussion and analysis is intended to highlight and supplement data and information presented elsewhere in this report, including the consolidated financial statements and related notes and should be read in conjunction with the accompanying tables and our financial statements included in this report. The consolidated financial statements and notes have been prepared in accordance with GAAP. Certain statements in this discussion and analysis may be deemed to include "forward-looking statements" and are based on management's current expectations and are subject to uncertainty and changes in circumstances. Forward-looking statements are not historical facts but instead represent only management's belief regarding future events, many of which by their nature are inherently uncertain and outside of management's control. Actual results may differ materially from those included in these statements due to a variety of factors, including worldwide and local economic conditions, success in business retention and obtaining new business and other factors. Factors that could cause these differences are discussed in the sections titled "Cautionary Note Regarding Forward-Looking Statements" and "Risk Factors." For management's considerations and determinations of each non-core item discussed, please see "Reconciliation of Non-GAAP Financial Measures".

We are a full service bank and wealth manager headquartered in Hamilton, Bermuda. We operate our business through our four reportable segments, three geographical and one other: Bermuda, Cayman, Channel Islands and the UK, and Other. We offer banking services, comprising of retail and corporate banking, and wealth management, which consists of trust, private banking, and asset management. In our Bermuda and Cayman segments, we offer retail banking and wealth management. In our Channel Islands and the UK segment, we offer retail and corporate banking and wealth management. The Other segment includes our operations in the jurisdictions of The Bahamas, Canada, Mauritius, Singapore and Switzerland. In these jurisdictions we either provide wealth management or operate service centers. These jurisdictions individually and collectively do not meet the quantitative threshold for segmented reporting and are therefore aggregated as a non-reportable operating segment.

Our business is affected by international, regional and local economic conditions as well as, the perception of future economic prospects. The significant macro-economic factors that impact our business include the US and global economic landscapes, unemployment rates, the housing markets and interest rates. 2025 began with elevated uncertainty in financial markets as a new administration came into office in the US. Tariffs, fiscal deficits, elevated inflation, and the threat of reduced global trade briefly destabilized sovereign bond and equity markets across the globe. Since that time, as the US tariff threat has lessened, and the US Federal Reserve along with other global central banks, has further eased monetary policy, volatility has declined significantly. While the issues listed above remain threats to growth in 2026, markets appear better equipped to handle the uncertainty. In addition, slightly slower growth and some disinflationary pressures will likely give global central banks room to further ease financial conditions at the margin. Nevertheless, sovereign yield curves and longer-term risk premia are likely to remain elevated for some time.

Bermuda's economy grew 1.9% in 2024 and Real GDP was 10% higher than when compared to 2019 levels of GDP, indicating that Bermuda has recovered from the COVID-19 pandemic economic impacts and has experienced growth.

The international business sector, especially the life reinsurance and captive insurance markets, continue to grow, attracting new capital and companies, demonstrated by employment levels reaching new highs of 5,040 employed in the international business sector in 2024. This is an increase of 1,020 from 2019 levels and currently represents

15% of total employment in Bermuda. Bermuda remains the world's largest captive domicile, one of the largest markets for reinsurance underwriting and the largest market for insurance-linked securities.

Retail activity continues to be challenged and consumer imports via online retailers remain at elevated levels. While the official inflation rates recorded in Bermuda have been modest, general cost of living challenges remain, driven by food costs, energy costs and housing costs, both in rental rates and building costs.

Airlift increased by just over 1.2% in 2025, however, several hurricane related impacts caused a reduction in air and cruise arrivals for the year, with air arrivals down 1.65% and cruise arrivals down 14.6%. There continues to be positive news on hotel developments, with two hotels, including the largest in Bermuda, currently undergoing redevelopment. Recent hotel operating performance has been strong, with revenue per available room night in 2025 of $413 compared to $379 in 2024, driven by stable occupancy trends (64.0% compared to 63.2% in 2024) and increasing average daily rates of $611 compared to $554 in 2024.

Butterfield & Son Bank Act, 1904》（"Butterfield Act"）設立。本公司已於百慕達公司註冊處註冊，註冊編號為LC 2106。本公司註冊辦公室及主要營運辦公室位於百慕達漢密爾頓市65號Front Street，郵遞區號HM 12。本公司於美國的訴訟程序代理人為C T Corporation System，地址為紐約市28號Liberty Street，紐約10005。本公司電話號碼為(441) 295 1111。本公司維護網站地址為www.butterfieldgroup.com。本網站及本網站上或可存取之資訊並未包含或納入本報告，亦非本報告之一部分。

N.T. Butterfield & Son Limited銀行的起源可追溯至1784年左右Nathaniel Butterfield所創立的貿易公司。1858年，本公司在百慕達設立為銀行，自那時起便對當地經濟的運作發揮重要作用。該銀行後於1904年依據當地議會特別法案設立。1960年代，隨著國際企業對百慕達經濟的貢獻大幅增加，本公司發展相關服務以滿足其需求。1967年，本公司在開曼羣島設立辦事處，至1980年代已擴展業務至零售銀行、投資管理及基金行政服務。1973年，本公司在根西島設立辦事處，以提供客戶使用英鎊貨幣的服務，因百慕達已離開英國英鎊區。此外，本公司為百慕達第一家銀行，於1980年代在百慕達設立首間ATM機器，並於2001年推出百慕達首項網際網路銀行服務。1971年，本公司於BSX交易所上市，股票代碼為"NTB.BH"。2016年，本公司於紐約證券交易所上市，股票代碼為"NTB"。
2008年及2009年，因全球金融危機的影響，本公司因投資組閤中美國非機構抵押貸款支持證券所致的損失，以及對本地市場旅遊業貸款的減記而產生損失。為彌補這些損失，該銀行於2009年6月發行了價值2億美元的優先股。2009年及2010年，本公司實施一項全面的重整計畫：聘請新的管理團隊、降低資產負債表風險，並從一組投資者及現有股東處籌集了5.5億美元的普通股資金。
自重整以來，本公司已採取策略專注於銀行及財富管理的核心業務。我們透過退出非核心市場、重新定位資產負債表、投資效率提升計畫，以及持續投資核心業務線以實現內生成長及透過收購成長，來落實此策略。透過遵循此策略，我們已改善財務表現，並能啟動對投資者的漸進資本回饋政策。以下為執行此策略的最新關鍵步驟：

•2017年10月，本公司與德意志銀行（"Deutsche Bank"）簽訂協議，以淨現金支付2,470萬美元取得德意志銀行（"Deutsche Bank"）的全球信託解決方案（"GTS"）業務，不包括其美國業務。交易完成後，Butterfield接管GTS投資組合的持續管理與行政作業，該投資組合約有1,000個信託結構，服務約900位私人客戶，位於根西島、瑞士、開曼羣島及新加坡。作為交易的一部分，本公司亦取得馬達加斯加的一家服務公司，以提供信託業務的運作與支援服務。此交易於2018年3月完成。
•2018年2月，本公司與德意志銀行簽訂協議，取得德意志銀行在開曼羣島及英屬_Channel Islands_的銀行及保管業務，該業務主要服務金融中介機構及企業客戶。該銀行於2018年開始納入與該收購相關的客戶存款，並於2019年上半年完成此納入作業。
•2018年5月，本公司發行價值7,500萬美元的5.25%固定轉浮動利率次級債券，到期日為2028年，用以償還部分現有債務，並用於其他一般企業用途。
•於2022年9月，本公司與Credit Suisse全球信託業務簽訂協議，取得其在新加坡、根西島及巴哈馬運作的資產。該交易於2023年12月完成。
•於2023年6月，本公司執行了銀行$75 百萬美元 5.25% 固定轉浮動利率次級債券之提前贖回，該債券到期日為2028年6月1日。

•2024年，Butterfield在Channel Islands的業務進行重整，使得原先由Butterfield Bank (Jersey) Limited在Jersey或從Jersey進行的所有業務，已轉移至Butterfield Bank (Guernsey) Limited透過其Jersey分行（Butterfield Bank (Guernsey) Limited, Jersey Branch）進行。此方案已於2024年5月14日經Jersey王室法院批准，業務轉移於2024年6月1日生效。

paragraphs: 本節說明管理階層對本公司財務狀況及營運成果的觀點。以下討論與分析旨在強調並補充本報告其他部分所呈現的資料與資訊，包括合併財務報表及相關附註，應與附表及本報告所包含的財務報表一併閱讀。合併財務報表及附註係依照美國通用會計準則（GAAP）編製。本討論與分析中某些陳述可能被視為包含「預測性陳述」，並基於管理階層目前的預期，且受不確定性及情況變動的影響。預測性陳述並非歷史事實，而是管理階層對未來事件的信念，許多事件本質上具有內在不確定性，且超出管理階層的控制範圍。實際結果可能因多種因素而與這些陳述中所包含的結果有重大差異，包括全球及地方經濟狀況、業務留存成功與取得新業務的成效及其他因素。導致這些差異的因素於「預測性陳述警示」及「風險因素」節中討論。有關管理階層對每項非核心項目之考量與決定，請參閱「非GAAP財務指標之彙整」。

本公司為總部設於百慕達漢密爾頓的全方位銀行與資產管理機構。我們透過四大應報告分部運作業務，三個地理區與一個其他分部：百慕達、開曼羣島、通道羣島與英國，以及其他。我們提供銀行服務，包含零售與企業銀行，以及資產管理服務，包含信託、私人銀行與資產管理。在百慕達與開曼羣島分部，我們提供零售銀行與資產管理服務。在通道羣島與英國分部，我們提供零售與企業銀行服務與資產管理服務。其他分部包含我們在巴哈馬、加拿大、毛里求斯、新加坡與瑞士等司法管轄區的運作。在這些司法管轄區，我們提供資產管理服務或運作服務中心。這些司法管轄區個別及整體均未達到分部報告的量化門檻，因此被歸類為非應報告運作分部。

本公司業務受國際、區域及地方經濟條件以及對未來經濟前景的觀感所影響。對本公司業務有重大影響的總體經濟因素包括美國與全球經濟環境、失業率、住宅市場及利率。2025年以美國新政府上任為起點，財務市場出現較高的不確定性。關稅、財政赤字、高通貨膨脹以及全球貿易減少的威脅，短暫地使全球國債與股權市場陷入動盪。自那時起，隨著美國關稅威脅減緩，以及美國聯邦儲備銀行與其他全球央行進一步放寬貨幣政策，市場波動已顯著降低。雖然上述問題在2026年仍為成長的威脅，但市場似乎更能應對不確定性。此外，略為減緩的成長與一些通縮壓力，將為全球央行進一步放寬財務條件提供空間。然而，國債收益率曲線與長期風險 premiums 可能會在一段時間內保持較高水平。
百慕達經濟在2024年成長1.9%，實際GDP較2019年的GDP水平高出10%，顯示百慕達已從 COVID-19 疫情的經濟衝擊中復甦，並經歷成長。
國際業務部門，特別是人壽再保險與設立保險公司的市場，持續成長，吸引新資本與公司，這由國際業務部門就業人數達到5,040人的新高可見一斑，較2019年的水平增加1,020人，目前佔百慕達總就業人數的
15%。百慕達仍是全球最大的設立保險公司註冊地，也是再保險承保最大的市場之一，並為保險聯結證券最大的市場。
零售活動持續受到挑戰，消費者透過線上零售商進口的產品仍維持較高水平。雖然百慕達官方記錄的通貨膨脹率相對溫和，但生活成本的挑戰依然存在，主要由食品成本、能源成本及住房成本所驅動，包括租金率與建築成本。

2025年航空運輸量僅成長約1.2%，然而，幾場颶風相關影響導致該年度航空與遊輪抵達人數減少，航空抵達人數減少1.65%，遊輪抵達人數減少14.6%。酒店開發方面持續有正面消息，目前有兩家酒店，包括百慕達最大的酒店，正在進行重建。近期酒店營運表現強勁，2025年的每間可用客房每晚收入為224 百萬美元，較2024年的224 百萬美元有所成長，這是由於穩定的入住率（64.0% 較2024年的63.2%）以及平均每日房價提高（611 美元 較2024年的554 美元）所驅動。

headings: 與我們營運市場相關的風險
總體經濟因素，包括區域衝突，及其他地緣政治事件，可能幹擾我們的業務，並對我們的財務狀況或營運結果產生不利影響。
百慕達及開曼羣島的旅遊業衰退，可能對我們的業務、財務狀況或營運結果產生不利影響。
我們營運的某些司法管轄區域，包括百慕達、根西島及澤西島，擁有存款保險制度或存款補償制度，因此我們持續產生相關成本。
極端天氣、自然災害及氣候變遷的潛在影響，可能幹擾我們的業務，並對我們的財務狀況或營運結果產生不利影響。
我們營運的大多數市場，並沒有系統性的信用局報告。
與我們戰略、品牌、產品組合及其他業務方面相關的風險
我們依賴我們的聲譽及品牌對客戶的吸引力。任何對我們聲譽及品牌吸引力的損害，可能對我們及我們的業務前景造成傷害。
通貨膨脹的影響，以及利率波動，已並可能持續對我們的淨利息-margin 以及利潤率產生負面影響。
高漲的通貨膨脹水平可能對我們的財務表現造成風險。
我們的貸款及投資組合面臨提前償還的風險，這可能對我們產生重大不利影響。
我們投資組閤中的證券價值可能在未來下降。
外幣交換率的波動水平及變動可能影響我們的業務、財務狀況及營運成果。
若我們無法有效地管理流動性，我們可能需要尋求額外融資，而我們的業務、財務狀況或營運成果可能受到不利影響。
我們依賴第三方提供對我們日常運作至關重要的服務，若這些第三方無法令人滿意地履行其義務，可能對我們產生負面影響。
我們在業務的各方面都面臨競爭，我們可能無法在目前水平吸引並留住財富管理、信託及銀行客戶。
新增產品與服務，或修改後的產品與服務，可能使我們面臨實作風險，並損害我們的聲譽。
paragraphs: 本公司管理階層認為影響我們的主要風險與不確定性已於下文描述。任何下列風險，以及我們未知或目前認為不重要之風險，均可能對本公司之業務、財務狀況或營運成果造成重大不利影響。此外，下列風險因素包含警示聲明，識別出可能導致實際結果與本公司或代表本公司所作之預測性陳述顯著不同之重要因素。請參閱「預測性陳述之警示說明」。
在伯明翰、開曼羣島、通道羣島及英國等市場，以及本公司營運之其他市場，不利之經濟與市場條件，過去曾導致並可能在未來導致營收減少、資產品質下降、提列更多撥備及獲利減少。

本公司之財務表現，特別是借款人支付貸款利息及償還貸款本金之能力，以及用以擔保這些貸款之資產價值，以及對我們所提供貸款及其他產品與服務之需求，這些都是我們未來成長所倚賴之因素，均高度依賴我們營運市場之商業環境。若伯明翰、開曼羣島、通道羣島或英國等市場出現衰退，將對本公司之業務表現產生深遠影響。影響本公司財務表現之商業環境要素包括短期與長期利率、任何與我們信用評級相關之國家信用評級遭降級、現行收益率曲線、通貨膨脹與價格水平、貨幣與財政政策、規範或法律變動（包括稅務、不動產與居所法規與規則之變動或執行方式之變動）、課徵關稅或報復性關稅、失業率、投資者或企業信心、天然或人為災難、我們營運市場之地方經濟強度，或這些或其他因素之組合。例如，2025年穆迪將美國長期外幣發債者違約評級從「AAA」降為「Aa1」，2023年惠譽評級服務將美國長期外幣發債者違約評級從「AAA」降為「AA+」，此一評級變動影響了銀行持有美國政府國庫券及美國政府機構發行之房貸擔保證券之評級。任何進一步之降級可能進一步影響由美國聯邦政府發行或擔保之證券之穩定性，以及我們投資證券組合之價值或流動性，並可能導致我們之交易對手要求我們貸款之額外擔保品。
不利之市場條件可能導致借款人信用品質惡化、我們產品與服務之需求減少、貸款逾期數量增加、違約與核銷數量增加、貸款損失提列額增加、資產價值下降、投資表現惡化，並對我們貸款組合之品質造成整體重大不利影響。
與更具地理分散性之銀行不同，本公司業務主要集中於伯明翰、開曼羣島、通道羣島及英國，因此我們可能比更具分散性之競爭對手更容易受到這些市場衰退之影響。

本公司之銀行業務集中於伯明翰、開曼羣島及通道羣島與英國，並為這些市場之客戶提供服務。截至2025年12月31日，我們總淨營收中有43%、31%及18%分別來自伯明翰、開曼及通道羣島與英國應報告分部。此外，截至2025年12月31日，我們在伯明翰、開曼及通道羣島與英國所發放之貸款分別佔33%、23%及44%。因此，這些市場若出現衰退，可能對本公司之銀行業務產生深遠影響。此外，本公司已致力於擴展核心業務線，包括透過收購方式。若本公司無法成功擴展核心業務線、成功整合收購或這些市場對我們核心服務之需求減少（包括因聲譽受損之觀感、這些管轄區活動之監管審查增加或其他原因），可能對本公司之業務與營運成果造成不利影響，包括對任何收購之業務之持續成功造成影響。
